text:
Here's a different take. This one is shorter and leads with the "why it matters" angle; the earlier version was more of a spec rundown.

---

# LinkedIn Post

**Several closed frontier models scored near zero on a real-world security test. They didn't fail. They refused to try.**

The test, part of the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index, asks a model to reproduce a real vulnerability in open-source software and then patch it.

Mistral's new open-weight model, **Mistral Large 4** (nicknamed "Le Chonk" 🇫🇷), scored **82%**, the highest reported score on that test in the index.

Here's why that matters: **you can't fix what you can't reproduce.**

For security teams, the problem with closed APIs isn't only capability. Legitimate defensive work, like incident response, vulnerability research, and malware analysis, often looks like an attack to a content filter. And if your provider cuts access mid-incident, you're stuck.

Open weights change that:
→ You control the deployment
→ You set the usage policy
→ You can fine-tune on your own code, logs, and samples
→ You can audit refusal behavior yourself rather than take a vendor's word for it

It's not a free-for-all, either. On cyber prompts from JailbreakBench, StrongREJECT, and AgentHarm, its average refusal rate is higher than any other open-weight model's.

**Quick facts:**
• ~1T parameter MoE, with ~49B active per the announcement
• 1M token context
• Text + image input
• 93% on Cybench and 93.3% prompt-injection resistance on Lakera's B3
• Top-5 open-weights model on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index
• Day-0 support in Transformers, vLLM, llama.cpp, and TRL

The 2-bit quant even runs on a single Mac Studio–class machine with 512GB of unified memory.

Capable open models are becoming a real option for defenders. That's a shift worth watching.

Security folks: would you run a model like this in-house? 👇

#Cybersecurity #AI #OpenSource #InfoSec #LLM #MistralAI #HuggingFace

---

**Notes:**
- The same caveat applies: the article says ~49B active parameters, but the model ID says A52B. It's worth checking the model card.
- The model's license (Mistral Ecosystem Open-Weight License) restricts model-as-a-service offerings. You might mention that if your audience includes companies thinking about hosting it commercially.

I can also make it shorter, more technical, or more casual if you'd like.
